title: Light of the Gentile Nations
description: Light of the Gentile Nations in Tonic Solfa to GREENLAND, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Johann Franck wrote these words in German. Catherine Winkworth's translation was printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 190.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens and Sixes Double (7.6.7.6.7.6.7.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to GREENLAND; any other Sevens and Sixes Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: Light of the Gen-tile na-tions, Thy peo-ple’s Joy and Love! Drawn by Thy Spir-it hith-er, We glad-ly come to prove Thy pre-sence in Thy tem-ple And seek with ear-nest mind, As Sime-on once had wait-ed His Sa-vior God to find.

lines: Yea, Lord, Thy servants meet Thee,
Where Thy true Word hath promised
That they should see Thy face.
Thou yet wilt gladly grant us,
In faith’s strong arms to bear Thee,
Be Thou our Joy, our Brightness,
That shines mid pain and loss,
Our Sun in times of terror,
Let us, O Lord, be faithful
Since I have seen my Savior,
Now with the eye of faith;
No foe of Thee can rob me,
As Thou dost dwell in me,
No pain, no death, has terrors
To part my soul from Thee.
Lord, here on earth Thou seemest
At times to frown on me,
And through my tears I often

licence: Public domain: Johann Franck died in 1677; Catherine Winkworth died in 1878.
credits: Words by Johann Franck (1618–1677), translated by Catherine Winkworth (1827–1878), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to GREENLAND by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
